title: Google Stock Investors Biggest Risk | GOOG Stock Deep Dive Part 3
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA examines the biggest risk to Alphabet: the transition from traditional search results into AI Mode and AI Overviews, which he compares to Disney's move from cable to streaming - move too fast and you lose the cash flow of the old business, too slow and you fall behind on consumer behaviour. The good news, he argues, is monetisation: chief business officer Philipp Schindler (rendered 'Philip' in captions) said Alphabet is now scaling high-quality ads within AI Overviews and AI Mode to more users and queries, expanding into international markets, and that both surfaces are 'significantly under-monetised' - so Search growth should improve as ads ramp. He is surprised YouTube Premium has only just over 150 million subscribers versus Netflix's 300 million-plus, despite YouTube dominating viewing time and growing engagement faster - a sign most YouTube viewing is ad-supported. Netflix is a large position in his portfolio and one of his best-ranked stocks; he wonders whether Netflix should offer a completely free, ad-supported tier. No explicit buy, hold or sell rating and no fair value is stated in this video, so no call-event is recorded; his tracked GOOGL stance remains BUY (31 October).
